statement.p: Consider the vector field \vec{F} shown in the figure below together with the paths C_1, C_2, and C_3.

image.shortdescription: A horizontal vector field with three linear segment paths

description.p: Graph of a constant vector field pointing horizontally to the right. Curve C1 is a diagonal line with length 1.67 extending from the left of of the graph near the midline up 1.5 units and to the right 0.75 units. The vector field points with constant length horizontally to the left Curve C2 is a vertical line extending from a point to the right side of the graph upwards 1.5 units. The vector field points with constant length horizontally to the left Curve C3 is a horizontal line segment with a length 1.5, extending along the bottom of the graph from right to left. The vector field points with constant length horizontally to the left

p.em: (Note: For the vector field, vectors are shown with a dot at the tail of the vector.)

statement.p: Arrange the line integrals \int_{C_1} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r}, \int_{C_2} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r} and \int_{C_3} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r} in ascending order:

?
integral on C1
integral on C2
integral on C3 \lt
?
integral on C1
integral on C2
integral on C3 \lt
?
integral on C1
integral on C2
integral on C3 .

static.solution:
\int_{C_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec r > 0, because the curve moves from left to right, in the same direction as the vector field.
Applying this logic to each of the curves, we find that \int_{C_{3}}\vec F\cdot\vec r \lt \int_{C_{2}}\vec F\cdot\vec r \lt \int_{C_{1}}\vec F\cdot\vec r.
